title: Renovate native method binding
body:
### Tested versions

Godot `4.6.1` and godot-cpp `10.0.0-rc1` but this is present in practically the entire git history 

### System information

Arch Linux

### Issue description

I was trying to implement method binding with lambdas in godot-cpp when I've noticed that the rabbit hole goes deeper. In resumi, native method binding in Godot, at least for the C++ language, relies on method delegates, more specifically in fast delegates, which store a pointer for it to then be delegated a corresponding native call from the engine. Of course I wouldn't have any luck with that but I've picked up on that there are certain drawbacks with the implementation in Godot.

First of, the implementation uses casts of member function pointers in a way that can result undefined behavior per what godotengine/godot-cpp#1586 documents. It might sound that I'm making a grand deal out of this, but consider what the code does.

```cpp
// core/object/method_binding

MethodBind *create_method_bind(R (T::*p_method)(P...)) {
#ifdef TYPED_METHOD_BIND
  MethodBind *a = memnew((MethodBindWhateverTypeOfFunction<T, P...>)(p_method));
#else
  MethodBind *a = memnew((MethodBindWhateverTypeOfFunction<P...>)(reinterpret_cast<void (MB_T::*)(P...)>(p_method)));
#endif // TYPED_METHOD_BIND
  a->set_instance_class(T::get_class_static());
  return a;
}
```

Here `MB_T` is a type alias to a forward declaration of a non existing class if `TYPED_METHOD_BIND` is not defined. In theory this wouldn't be a problem if one class derives from another, but here is an enormous issue in case the compiler gets confounded while reinterpreting casts or at runtime where things could be as helpless as well. Can happen with older C++ toolchain versions or that one which required a point release. This might be the one case that MSVC does it right by giving out an error. Besides C++ implementation jabbering, I think that these casts were done for better, more performant codegen.

The other thing is that `MethodBind` could use newer mechanisms such as `std::function` or something with potentially much less penalty. While storing function pointers is not a bad thing by itself, there could be room for improvement for short or relatively trivial methods if lambdas could be used instead. These can be inlined as well as being convenient to use on the spot instead of defining yet another function.

All of this is not to criticize `MethodBind` baselessly, as its implementation has probably more than 15 years and still holds up to this day, but to say that this place might need a little bit more of attention. It was written in those days where there was no `std::function` and fast delegates were the best option out there. Today the language is, gracefully, smarter with this things so something better can be done.

I did not open a proposal because we are dealing with undefined behavior and C++ shenanigans.

### Steps to reproduce

Maybe running `clang-tidy` or compiling with MSVC without the `TYPED_METHOD_BIND` preprocessor definition.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A as this pertains to engine development.
